subject: DPA: derivative stewardship, subprocessor tiering, and model-improvement opt-out
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@goodhealthsys.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: GoodHealth Systems Legal <legal@goodhealthsys.com>
Date: 2025-11-28T14:05:00Z
Subject: DPA redline + clarifications on training & subprocessors

Hi David,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We're pushing final DPA redlines through procurement and legal — attached is our current edit (GoodHealth-DPA-redlines.pdf). A few high-priority items your team asked to review: 

1) No-training / model-improvement: we need an explicit, enforceable commitment that GoodHealth customer interaction data (prompts, responses, session transcripts) will not be used to train or improve any public or shared models unless we opt in in writing. We understand platform telemetry for service reliability is different, but we need boundaries and a definition of what counts as "model improvement".

2) Prompt/response ownership: the DPA asks that customers retain rights to outputs derived from their data and that Redwood will not claim derivative IP over customer prompts+responses. Please confirm operational controls you would rely on to respect this (e.g., data segregation, ephemeral KV, exportability).

3) Subprocessor tiers: we need a clear list of subprocessors and an explicit tiering (primary vs downstream subcontractors). For any subcontractors that could access raw prompts/responses, we need either: (a) onshore processing, or (b) KMS controls + attestation + a path to evidence logs on request.

4) Evidence requests + timeline: procurement needs a short evidence pack for SOC2 scope items and examples of the export/evidence flow (logs, proof of deletion, sftp/export modes). If you can provide a one-page operational summary and a time estimate to deliver a fuller evidence pack, that will help procurement sign off.

We're aiming to close contracting by the week starting Dec 8. Can you confirm what you can commit to now vs. what requires engineering work?

Attaching: GoodHealth-DPA-redlines.pdf

Warmly,
Samantha Lee
Head of Legal Operations
GoodHealth Systems
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@goodhealthsys.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-11-28T16:10:00Z
Subject: Re: DPA redline + clarifications on training & subprocessors

Samantha — thanks for the clear notes and the redline. Quick summary of what we can do immediately and what will need a short operational/engineering runbook: 

Immediate (can be contractually committed today):
- No-training: Redwood can commit that customer interaction data will not be used to train or improve Redwood public/shared models without explicit written opt-in from the customer. We will add a defined clause in the DPA: "No model improvement or training on Customer Data without Customer's written consent."
- Prompt/response ownership: we can accept language that the customer retains ownership of outputs generated from their data; Redwood will not claim derivative IP over customer prompts and responses.
- Subprocessor enumerations: we will provide the current list of subprocessors and mark which services are storage, compute, telemetry, or model infra.

Requires operational follow-up (we can provide evidence and tooling within 7–10 business days):
- Evidence pack: we will produce an evidence summary (configurable export, sample audit logs, KMS footprint) for the SOC2-relevant items and dataflow diagrams.
- Subprocessor tiering: we will produce an explicit mapping of primary vs downstream subcontractors and highlight where customer content could traverse. For any subprocessor that processes raw prompts/responses, we will indicate residency/KMS options.

Implementation notes 
- Hosted vs Dedicated: for customers that require stronger guarantees (onshore processing, strict subprocessor limits), Dedicated or Private deployments are the path we recommend; Hosted customers can choose SFTP/API export plus contractual no-training, but there will be operational caveats we will spell out.

Next steps:
1) Kimberly will propose redline language to incorporate the no-training and ownership clauses.
2) We'll deliver a 1-page evidence summary and a project ETA for the deeper evidence pack (target 7 business days).
3) If GoodHealth needs onshore-only subprocessors for certain flows, we can scope a Dedicated pilot and provide a cost/lead estimate.

I'll flag Kimberly and Marissa to take the drafting and operations pieces.

—David
David Kim
Head of Privacy & Data Governance
Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@goodhealthsys.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-11-29T09:23:00Z
Subject: Re: DPA redline + clarifications on training & subprocessors

Hi Samantha — looping in with proposed language and a couple clarifying asks before we redline the PDF: 

Proposed contract-friendly snippets (draft for DPA):
- No-Training: "Provider will not use Customer Data (including prompts, responses, transcripts, or derivatives thereof) to train, fine-tune, or improve Provider models that are shared across customers, unless Customer provides prior written consent."
- Outputs: "Customer retains ownership and all intellectual property rights in Outputs generated from Customer Data. Provider will not claim derivative ownership of Customer Data or Outputs."

Clarifying asks:
- Could you identify which GoodHealth roles need access to the evidence pack (legal vs. procurement vs. security)? We can tailor the level of operational detail accordingly.
- On the subprocessor tiers: would GoodHealth accept a signed attestation for downstream subcontractors and on-demand logs (rather than rearchitecting for onshore-only) as a middle ground? If not, we need to scope Dedicated deployment.

Attachments: evidence-pack-summary.xlsx (high-level mapping of logs and artifacts we can provide). I'll push a redline of the DPA with the snippets above once we hear back on access.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@goodhealthsys.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-12-01T11:02:00Z
Subject: Re: DPA redline + clarifications on training & subprocessors

Samantha — operational follow-up and timeline from Product/PS perspective: 

- Evidence pack ETA: we can deliver the one-page operational summary by EOD Dec 4 and the fuller evidence pack (sample audit logs, KMS mapping, export flow) by Dec 11. That will include: audit examples (access logs, deletion proofs), a table of subprocessors and roles, and the export/SFTP vs API options.
- Onshore requirement: if GoodHealth requires no downstream subcontracting outside the US for prompt/response storage or processing, we should scope a Dedicated pilot. Quick numbers: dedicated pilot (3 months) ~ 6–8 weeks to provision; procurement will want a TCO and SLA.
- DocuSign: we can pre-populate the DPA redline once Kimberly confirms language. I'll attach a preliminary MOA for the Dedicated pilot for internal review.

Attachments: signed-MOA.pdf (placeholder for mutual ops agreement we discussed).

Would you be available for a 30-minute sync next week (Dec 8–10) so we can walk through the evidence pack and the procurement checklist?

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Lead, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@goodhealthsys.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-12-01T15:30:00Z
Subject: Re: DPA redline + clarifications on training & subprocessors

Thanks all — this is helpful. Procurement and security will want the one-page summary first; legal will want the contract snippets in redline. A few quick items: 

- Access to evidence: please send the one-page summary to legal@goodhealthsys.com and secops@goodhealthsys.com.
- Temporary attestation: procurement said a signed attestation that Redwood will not use GoodHealth customer data for model improvement for 12 months from sign date is acceptable if followed by the evidence pack. Could you confirm we can provide that?
- Sync: Dec 9 at 10:00am ET works for our team. Please send calendar invite and preferred dial-in.

I'll loop in procurement on the invite and upload the DPA redline to the HubSpot record. Thanks again — if you can get the one-pager to us by Dec 4 we're aligned on timeline.

Best,
Samantha Lee
Head of Legal Operations
GoodHealth Systems
